# Envelope test vectors

`vectors.json` is the published wire-format vector set for `parley/msg/v1`.
Changing it is a wire-format change.

## What is in it

Fixed keys: Ed25519 sender seed `0x11 * 32`, X25519 recipient prekey scalar
`0x22 * 32`. For each vector (`task`, `result`, `status-empty-rpk`):

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `header` | deterministic header encoding (below) |
| `header_hash` | SHA-256(header); used as both HPKE `info` and `aad` |
| `enc`, `ciphertext` | HPKE encapsulated key and AEAD ciphertext |
| `transcript` | `header \|\| SHA-256(u32(len enc) \|\| enc \|\| u32(len ct) \|\| ct)` |
| `signature` | Ed25519(sender key, transcript); deterministic |
| `message` | wire message: four `u32`-length-prefixed fields: header, enc, ciphertext, signature |

Suite: DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256, ChaCha20-Poly1305, HPKE base
mode (RFC 9180 ids 0x0020, 0x0001, 0x0003). It is fixed and carried inside the
signed header; there is no negotiation.

Header encoding, all integers big-endian: `field(label="parley/msg/v1")`,
`u16 kem, u16 kdf, u16 aead`, `field(tenant)`, `field(sender device)`,
`field(sender key id)`, `u64 binding version`, `field(target device)`,
`field(prekey id)`, `field(task id, 16 bytes)`, `field(context id)`,
`u64 seq`, `u8 type` (1 TASK, 2 STATUS, 3 INPUT_REQUIRED, 4 RESULT, 5 ERROR, 6 CANCEL, 7 REPLY), `u64 issued_at`, `u64 expiry` (unix seconds),
`field(rpk)`, `field(prev hash)`, `field(prekey object)`; `field(x)` is
`u32 len || x`. `prev hash` is the `header_hash` of the previous message in the
task (the `result` vector chains to the `task` vector).

## Reproducibility

HPKE draws a fresh ephemeral key per seal, so `enc` and `ciphertext` are one
sample and cannot be regenerated byte for byte. Everything else is
deterministic. Checking is therefore done in two independent ways:

1. `go test ./internal/envelope` (`TestPublishedVectors`) re-encodes each
   header from its fields, recomputes the hash and transcript, re-signs and
   compares the signature byte for byte, verifies, and opens.
2. `verify_vectors.py` shares no code with the Go package. It parses the header
   itself, rebuilds hash, transcript and framing, verifies the signature, and
   decrypts with its own RFC 9180 key schedule built on the `cryptography`
   package:

   ```
   python3 -m venv /tmp/v && /tmp/v/bin/pip install cryptography
   /tmp/v/bin/python internal/envelope/testdata/verify_vectors.py
   ```

## Regenerating

```
PARLEY_UPDATE_VECTORS=1 go test ./internal/envelope -run TestPublishedVectors
```

Rewrites `vectors.json` with a new sample seal (new `enc`, `ciphertext`,
`transcript`, `signature`, `message`). Regenerate only for an intentional
format change, then rerun both checks above and the fuzz seeds below.

## Fuzz corpus

`fuzz/FuzzMessage/` is the committed seed corpus (the vector messages and
headers, plus truncated and trailing-byte variants). `go test` replays it;
CI also fuzzes for a short time:
`go test ./internal/envelope -run '^$' -fuzz FuzzMessage -fuzztime 20s`.
